summary: P2 (standards): no committed test makes the drift check calls::problems fail. It only ever runs on the real table, so it is shown to pass and never shown to catch anything. The brief's I4-I6 check (eleven changes planted 'in the test' on the document Value and the table text) ran once as a throwaway and was not committed. a_document_the_table_does_not_describe_is_refused_by_the_table covers only Table::found, for one added rule (no row) and one changed rule set (other inputs). The following edits would keep CI green: dropping candidates, possibleValues, required or the searcher text from digest_of; judge_call no longer re-checking that a stored call breaks its rule; problems no longer reporting a row that no document declares. Fix: add one test that runs calls::problems on the committed text against each planted change and asserts a problem that names the remedy. The planted changes: an example word; a violate row and a pair row whose call breaks nothing; a deleted row; an undeclared row; the searcher text; the atip revision; a possibleValues, valueName, valueType or SAMPLES change. Blast radius: atip_check_order and arg_rules read the table on every push. The table is current today: CANON_BLESS_RULE_CALLS=1 at 24b8194a6 (115 s wall, 391 CPU-s) made it again and git diff --exit-code was 0.
